title: Spectral noisy-tenant quarantine, reservation recalculation, and burst-policy refactor
creator: Aisha Kaur
description:
Summary: A capacity incident on 2026-02-27 exposed a spectral noisy-tenant pattern where rapidly oscillating burst traffic exhausted ephemeral burst tokens while reservation accounting lagged behind actual usage. The result: eviction spikes, increased tail latency for adjacent tenants, and several Dedicated clusters hitting soft OOM/eviction cascades. This ticket captures the follow-up engineering work: a short-term quarantine flow for noisy tenants, a deterministic reservation recalculation heuristic to avoid under-provisioning, and a refactor of the burst-token governor to support graded degradation instead of binary cutoff. Goals: 1) Reduce cross-tenant tail-latency regressions during short-duration spikes; 2) Eliminate reservation drift windows > 60s that lead to mass evictions; 3) Ensure burst policy transitions are gradual and observable.

Scope: - Quarantine path: create an isolation state (named "spectral_quarantine") where tenants that breach a per-minute spectral-score are limited to a conservative baseline and moved to a temporary reserved bucket for fast diag and remediation. - Reservation recalculation: implement an online algorithm that blends short-term (30s) and long-term (15m) utilization with hysteresis and max-step caps to prevent oscillation. - Burst governor: replace current token-bucket hard cutoff with a multi-tier backoff that degrades concurrency and allows KV cache shedding before eviction. - Observability: add spectral scoring metrics, reservation-projection traces, and a dedicated dashboard for canary clusters. - Tests & rollout: synthetic spectral load harness, canary on two Dedicated pools, automatic rollback on increased customer errors.

Acceptance criteria: - Canary runs show <10% increase in median latency and no tail-latency spikes vs baseline under spectral load. - Reservation recompute never reduces allocated reservation by more than 20% in a single step. - Quarantine triggers are annotated in trace spans and surfaced in Console for operator action. - New burst governor feature gates behind runtime-1.24 flag and passes chaos-sim tests.
updates: 2026-03-02: Initial incident triage completed. Hypothesis: rapid alternating high- and low-qps patterns caused token-bucket exhaustion and a stale reservation window allowed mass eviction. Linked postmortem: https://confluence.redwood.ai/pages/INC-2026-02-27-dedicated-capacity-spectral-incident
2026-03-04: Prototype spectral_quarantine implemented in the allocator with feature flag. Local unit tests green. PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/allocator/pull/482

2026-03-06: Synthetic spectral load harness (spectral-synth) completed; runs reproduce eviction cascade at 60s horizon. Harness repo: https://github.com/redwood-inference/synthetic-loads/tree/main/spectral-synth

2026-03-08: Reservation recalculation algorithm v1 merged to feature branch. Performance regression bench shows stable steady-state but needs hysteresis tuning. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/reservation-service/pull/214

2026-03-09: Design review with Reliability and Product. Action: reduce single-step reservation delta to 20% and add 45s minimum dampening window. Notes: https://docs.google.com/document/d/1spectral-review-notes

2026-03-10: Burst governor refactor draft ready. Instead of hard token refusal, we now expose 3 backoff tiers (reduce concurrency, shed KV cache, soft-evict) with telemetry counters. Seeking Eng-Infra review. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/burst-governor/pull/7
2026-03-11: Canary plan approved. Two Dedicated pools reserved (canary-west-01, canary-eu-02). Metric SLOs and rollback thresholds defined in the Console runbook. Canary start scheduled 2026-03-15.

2026-03-12: Load run baseline complete. Observability dashboards created: https://console.redwood.ai/dashboards/spectral-incident. No security blockers found. Next: finalize rollout scripts and schedule on-call support during canary window.
notes: Work split across allocator, reservation-service, and burst-governor teams. Expect cross-team syncs twice weekly. Coordinate customer comms with TPM. Post-canalysis we will bake heuristics into autoscaler and Dedicated SLA playbook.
